text: {"overall_winner": "A", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Essay A organizes around three clear reasons (dangerous, causes problems, laziness) with a body paragraph for each and an introduction and conclusion", "quality": "Organized argumentative structure", "description": "The essay presents a clear thesis and develops each supporting point in its own paragraph within a recognizable introduction-body-conclusion framework."}, {"evidence": "Essay A quotes the article directly, e.g., \"when the vehicle is in danger of backing into an object\" and \"the technology fails and some is injured, who is at fault-the driver or the manufactuer?\"", "quality": "Use of textual evidence", "description": "The essay grounds its claims in specific details and quotations drawn from the source article."}, {"evidence": "Essay A states a firm, consistent position ('No, driverless cars should not be developed') and maintains it throughout", "quality": "Clear sustained position", "description": "The essay commits to a single stance and keeps every paragraph aligned with that position."}, {"evidence": "Essay A develops each reason with explanation and elaboration rather than just asserting it, e.g., explaining lawsuits and lost business from technology failure", "quality": "Reasoned elaboration", "description": "The essay extends each claim with concrete consequences and reasoning that build the argument."}, {"evidence": "Essay B wanders into personal anecdotes about family and car commercials and never commits to a clear position or develops reasons from the article", "quality": "Focused argumentation", "description": "Essay A stays on task arguing its thesis, whereas Essay B drifts into autobiography and vague musings rather than building a case."}]}
